messages:
tess: Heads up — seeing a sustained p99 jump in ORD (~18:16 UTC). From ~120ms to ~820ms across the pop. Charts show throughput drop too. Anyone oncall?

michael: I see it in the dashboard. Spike started ~18:12. Bulk of errors are timeouts from kernel selector fallback paths.

indra: Looking at runtime metrics — kernel_selector switched a bunch of hosts to the compatibility kernel around 18:11. kvcache evictions spiked at same time.

dave: Can you paste the host ids? I can ssh a few.

indra: Host list (from router traces): ord-r1-03, ord-r1-07, ord-r2-05 showed selector flips. kvcache.evictions/sec per host: ord-r1-03=420, ord-r1-07=390, ord-r2-05=610.

michael: Network hints: we saw increased RTT to upstream peering for those racks. RTT to ISP peer jumped ~60ms -> 210ms at 18:10. Could be path change/peering flap.

tess: @sre-bot can you run quick perf capture on ord-r2-05 and grab cpu steal / runqueue?

sre-bot: perf capture started on ord-r2-05 (pid 0). 10s window collecting.

(sre-bot posts): ```
# perf summary snippet
CPU  steal: 9.8%
runqueue: 2.1
freq avg: 1.3GHz (expected 2.2GHz)
softirq backlog: low
```

anika: 9.8% steal is high. That can change kernel micro-benchmarks and push selector to fallback. Any noisy tenants on those hosts?

michael: Aligning with infra logs — noisy-ml-job tenant hit ord-r2-05 around 18:08 with heavy host-side memcpy and cuda kernel warmups; tenant autoscaler also spawned 6 extra tasks.

dave: That explains CPU steal and freq scaling. But what about RTT / peering? Are these symptoms linked or two separate events?

indra: I correlated tracing: when kernel_selector falls back, batch sizes shrink (heuristic: kernel mismatch -> conservative batch). fewer tokens/req -> throughput drop -> more small open requests -> kvcache churn. So noisy tenant triggered kernel flip, but peering jitter amplified p99 because KV cache misses cause more network calls to state store. Both contributed.

tess: Can we pin kernel_selector on those hosts to the optimized kernel temporarily? What's risk?

michael: We can override selector to ignore performance score and prefer fast kernel for workloads that match model family. Risk: if the kernel is actually incompatible there could be rare correctness/regression. But short rollback window ok if we watch error rate.

anika: Immediate mitigations: 1) Evict noisy-ml-job from ord racks (coord w/ infra) 2) pin kernel selector to optimized kernel on ord-r1-*/ord-r2-* 3) increase kvcache capacity on those hosts by +15% 4) bump batch heuristic time_window from 8ms -> 12ms to avoid oscillation.

dave: I'm starting an eviction for noisy tenant now. infra ticket #INC-ORD-3742.

(15s later) sre-bot: eviction completed for noisy-ml-job on ord-r2-05.

michael: Pinning kernel selector override on ord-r1-03, ord-r1-07, ord-r2-05 via remote flag: ```
PATCH /runtime/hosts/selector
{
  "hosts": ["ord-r1-03","ord-r1-07","ord-r2-05"],
  "force_kernel": "fast-attn-v2",
  "ttl": 900
}
```

sre-bot: override applied. rolling restart not required; selector reloads config automatically.

indra: Increasing kvcache size via config: `kvcache.capacity_bytes += 15%` on affected hosts. Propagating now.

deploy-bot: rolling config change deployed to ord-r1-*, ord-r2-* (change id cfg-2024-ord-19).

michael: Also temporarily relaxing batching heuristic: `batcher.time_window_ms=12` for ord racks. Deploying.

deploy-bot: batcher config change live (id batch-cfg-ord-2024-19).

(2 minutes later) tess: Observability — p99 back down to ~140ms, kvcache.evictions/sec dropped under 40, kernel_selector stabilized to preferred kernel. Throughput trending up.

anika: Good. Any leftover network noise to monitor?

michael: Peering RTT has normalized to baseline ~55ms. ISP reported transient route flap with their upstream peer at 18:09-18:13. They applied fix.

dave: Follow-ups: 1) add alert when kernel_selector flip rate > 5 hosts / 1m 2) add guardrail that prevents selector fallback if CPU steal > 5% 3) investigate batching heuristic sensitivity to kvcache miss storms.

tess: Filed follow-ups: ENGRT-482 (selector flip alert), ENGRT-483 (selector guardrail), ENGRT-484 (batcher/kvcache tension).

michael: Nice work. Recommend a short postmortem note in incidents channel and mark as mitigated. :thumbsup:

tess: Will post summary in #incidents and mark resolved after 1h of stable metrics. Thanks everyone.

anika: Thanks — extra credit for the quick eviction call.

sre-bot: Incident marked mitigated (mitigation_ts=2198765488).
